findings.claim: The loop-8 residual sentence is much clearer. Two of its qualifiers can be read as narrower than the test's actual behaviour, and the solved-run record's not-covered list (coding-lab-solved-run.json line 49) uses the same wording. The private completed work could not be read in this session (the permission system denied access to the overlay), so I ran no solved or full-suite variant runs. Instead I ran the task 11 measurement block of layout.test.mjs (lines 125-249, executed verbatim through tests/browser.mjs withPage) on fresh copies of the untouched starter. Each copy had only one animation rule appended, and none sets a width. I printed each tag's unscaled flag and whether its drawn width equals its layout width, at both windows and both checklist widths, in 2 runs per page. (1) 'a paused, long-delayed or very long one that ends at the expected values passes' reads naturally as 'its end keyframe holds the expected values', and that is narrower than the behaviour. A paused animation, a long-delayed one with backwards fill and a days-long one, each holding a smaller scale on both tags with the default fill mode, read unscaled true with drawn width equal to layout width in all 4 measurements in 2 of 2 runs. Animation.finish() leaves no effect behind when nothing fills forwards. A real page draws those tags at the held scale. The same paused hold with forwards fill read unscaled false and drawn width unequal in 2 of 2 runs, which agrees with the loop-7 note that paused holds now fail: those holds kept their end value. So these animations pass unless the value they hold at their end is wrong. With the default fill, they pass whatever their keyframes say. The phrase is accurate only if 'ends at' means the element's state once the animation is over, so this is an ambiguity, not a false statement. (2) 'A finite animation is finished to its end whatever its play state or delay' is not scoped. Lines 137-144 finish animations only on .site-aside and the two tags. Elsewhere, finite animations are read at one moment, like endless ones, but the sentence names elements around the checklist only as a case of 'an endless one'. In the same harness, a finite 2-second scale pulse on .page that starts at its identity value and repeats 100000 times behaved like the endless version. In one run the drawn width differed from the layout width at the second window. In the other run it was equal at all four measurements. The endless version gave the same pattern. The earlier clause 'finite animations on them finished first' sets the scope implicitly. Graded low, as cl7-edu-002 was. This is maintainer and evidence text about the owner-accepted option A residual. README line 17 and task 11 Outcome, the text learners read, stay general and correct. The calculated width is still required.
findings.recommendation: Wording only, no test change, consistent with option A. In the lab.json notes and the next solved-run record, scope the first clause to the checklist and the two tags. Say that such an animation passes unless it holds a wrong value at its end, and that with the default fill mode nothing is held, so it passes whatever its keyframes. Say that every other animation, including finite ones on elements around the checklist, is read at one moment. Optionally add a default-fill paused scale hold to the matrix's list of variants that pass although forbidden.

items.note: Resolved by wording, as the reconciler accepted under the owner's option A. The test bytes are unchanged since 80eff5af (git diff --quiet 80eff5af 7e1a2af6 over tests/, README, starter/ and expected/). The lab.json notes now say that an animation still running is read at one moment, so an endless one 'can pass in some or all runs when it ... runs on an element around the checklist'. That names both the ancestor case and the run-to-run variation. The solved-run record's not-covered list (line 49 at 445137e2) says the same. As the brief asks, detection is not raised. The specific defects are fixed. The residual is now described by timing, not as 'width or padding' animations only. 'Paused' is qualified: finished whatever its play state or delay. Endless cases name width or padding, resting at none, the checklist's zoom and elements around the checklist. Animated custom properties are named. The 'rejects a non-identity transform ...' sentence now sits with 'It does not detect every animation that changes the drawn size', so held scale or zoom is no longer implied to be always caught. lab.json and the record's not-covered list agree. A narrower qualifier introduced in loop 8 ('that ends at the expected values') is filed as cl8-edu-001.

The private completed work could not be read in this session (the permission system denied access to the overlay), so I ran no solved or full-suite variant runs. The owner accepted this residual, so it is judged on how honestly it is stated. README bytes are unchanged since loop 6. Line 17 says 'It does not catch every animation, so task 11 also asks you to keep the checklist layout static'. Task 11 Outcome (line 141) scopes the static rule to the checklist, the two tags and the elements around them that affect their layout, and allows decorative effects elsewhere. Neither text tells learners that held or endless animations are acceptable, so the statement to learners is honest and fair. The maintainer-side wording is now much fuller. Its remaining imprecision is cl8-edu-001, which does not affect learners.
